title: Saudi Pipeline Attack Sends Oil Higher, AI Slowdown Hits Stocks
description:
Equities fell around the world after leaders of the biggest artificial-intelligence firms proposed slowing the technology’s development. 
Anthropic and OpenAI are promising measures to rein in the pursuit of cutting-edge AI models to better understand the risks posed by the technology following a series of security breaches. 

Oil pushed higher as Saudi Arabia’s closure of a major crude pipeline following attacks jolted the market, with the move disrupting a route that’s been key to bypassing the Strait of Hormuz during the US-Iran war. Meanwhile a planned meeting between Iran and several Gulf nations on creating a temporary shipping lane through the Strait has been postponed, according to Oman’s foreign minister.

Sweden’s election will go down to the wire, the tightest in its history, and one that will hinge on the complete counting in coming days of late-arriving ballots and votes from overseas.

Today's guests: Rachel Baxter, Vanguard European Head of Investment Management; Ayako Fujita, JPMorgan Chief Japan Economist; Cathryn Cluever Ashbrook, Bertelsmann Stiftung Senior Adviser


--
"The Pulse With Francine Lacqua" is all about conversations with high profile guests in the beating heart of global business, economics, finance and politics. Based in London, we go wherever the story is, bringing you exclusive interviews and market-moving scoops.
